title: Internal-Hom comparison for finite-Tor constructible inputs
statement:
Let $X$ be a finite-type $\overline{\mathbf F}_q$-scheme,
let $\nu_X:X_{\Proet}\to X_{\Et}$ be the site comparison,
let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X_{\Et},A_{E,n})$, and let
$M\in D^b_c(X_{\Et},A_{E,n})$. Then

$$
\nu_X^*R\mathcal Hom_A(K,M)\longrightarrow
R\mathcal Hom_A(\nu_X^*K,\nu_X^*M)
$$

is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $A=A_{E,n}$. Apply [lem-sf-hom-comparison-affine-inputs] to obtain a finite affine open cover $(j_i:U_i\hookrightarrow X)$ with every $U_i$ separated and of finite type over $k$. Write $K_i=K|_{U_i}$ and $M_i=M|_{U_i}$. The same lemma gives $K_i\in D^b_{ctf}(U_{i,\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $M_i\in D^b_c(U_{i,\mathrm{et}},A)$, retaining the cohomological and Tor bounds and the restricted flat models.

source.place: Proof, sentences 1-2: affine cover and preservation of the inputs

proof.text: For each $j_i$, restriction along $U_i$ is localization of either small site at $U_i$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]: an object over $U_i$ is exactly an etale, respectively weakly etale, $X$-object factoring through $U_i$, so $X_{\mathrm{et}}/U_i$ and $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/U_i$ are the small sites of $U_i$ and slice restriction is $j_{i,e}^*$, $j_{i,p}^*$. Apply the restriction clause of [lem-sf-site-hom-comparison-thick] with $T=X$, the finite ring $A$ and the etale object $U_i\to X$: under the canonical inverse-image comparison $j_{i,p}^*\nu_X^*\cong\nu_{U_i}^*j_{i,e}^*$ and the internal-Hom restriction isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] on both sites, $j_{i,p}^*(\beta_X)$ agrees with the specified evaluation transpose $\beta_{U_i,K_i,M_i}$ of [def-sf-evaluation-hom-site-comparison]. These identifications are isomorphisms, so $j_{i,p}^*(\beta_X)$ is invertible if and only if $\beta_{U_i,K_i,M_i}$ is.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: canonical-map compatibility under open restriction

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison] on each $U_i$. Step 1 supplies its separated finite-type and input hypotheses. Its coefficient is the same finite stage $A_{E,n}$ with $\ell\ne p$. The internal-Hom clause says exactly that $\beta_{U_i,K_i,M_i}$ is invertible; the dualizing-object and biduality clauses are not used. By step 2, $j_{i,p}^*\beta_X$ is invertible.

Finally fix $r\in\mathbf Z$ and apply $\mathcal H^r$ to $\beta_X$. Exact restriction commutes with these cohomology sheaves, so steps 2 and 3 give an inverse on every $U_i$. These inverses agree on overlaps by uniqueness of a two-sided inverse. For every pro-etale object $V\to X$, the opens $V\times_XU_i$ cover $V$; the sheaf axiom glues the local inverse maps uniquely, and their two composites are the identity since they are so on this cover. Therefore $\mathcal H^r(\beta_X)$ is an isomorphism for every $r$. The cohomology detection criterion [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], applied to the abelian category of pro-etale $A$-module sheaves, proves that $\beta_X$ itself is an isomorphism. If $X$ is empty the sheaf axiom for the empty covering gives the same conclusion, so the argument also covers the empty affine covering.
